findings.cause: Twenty inline tests and their private io_error fixture occupy 431 lines including registration, exceeding the repository inline unit-test guidance of about 300 lines.
findings.remedy: Move the existing test module body unchanged into crates/phantom/src/error/tests.rs and leave #[cfg(test)] mod tests; at the end of error.rs. The natural module path resolves it. Preserve super imports, private parent functions and all twenty method bodies. No #[path], new framework, production split or new test is needed.
findings.verification: Exact unchanged body/import and roster comparison plus targeted format; root compile and existing unit selection. This is placement, not a production file-size quota.

findings.cause: Private module declarations precede facade reexports; external reexports are interleaved after public profile/dns declarations. The standards put reexports with imports before module declarations.
findings.remedy: Group the existing reexports before declarations, retaining all cfg attributes, documentation, visibility and canonical public paths. Keep public profile/dns modules intact. No API change or crate split is required.
findings.verification: Mechanical exact item/cfg/path comparison, targeted format and root feature/doc compilation. A108 previously repaired route.rs; it is not full lib.rs evidence.

findings.category: documentation/category qualification, not confirmed transport defect
findings.cause: Resolve describes origin address resolution generally, but actual direct TCP DNS and dial failures share DirectConnectError::Connect, Http1TlsError::Connect and RequestErrorKind::Connect. The public category descriptions do not explain that phase distinction is unavailable on this path.
findings.remedy: Clarify Resolve/Connect rustdoc to describe the actual distinguished resolution failures and combined direct TCP setup category. Do not invent phase information, infer it from io::ErrorKind or change production retry classification without a separate contract decision.
findings.verification: An optional future controlled resolver failure through actual facade protocol choices can document observed categories, preserving typed sentinel cause. No new runtime reproduction or production defect is claimed here.

accepted_contracts: BuildError and RequestError store concrete typed causes; automatic Display/Debug exclude those causes, and RequestError Debug exposes only the path-free RequestOrigin and categorical fields
Source traversal for upload failure classification follows typed RequestBodyError rather than parsing messages; replay observations remain separate from policy, budgets and body eligibility
Remote H2 ConnectionError is specifically GOAWAY in its actual owner, while transport/local/reset cases remain distinct; this pass does not rerun vendor stream-id behavior

StatusError retains the complete unread response; bounded body/text/JSON helpers retain metadata and typed causes and drop failed data; JSON input limit explicitly does not promise an allocation budget
ResponseInfo Debug omits effective URI; metadata is attached by the actual request completion caller and cross-origin template stripping follows the real redirect path

Facade canonical request fields come from phantom_net::request and feature gates agree with the read manifest; full omits diagnostics and danger-disable-verification; public examples name currently exported functions/types
Template controls assert literal independent ordered name lists, value bytes and sensitivity flags at the expansion seam; required-protocol/trust/forwarding negatives have paired positives
A25 forwarding cache agreement and A26 Debug redaction remedies are present and protected; they are existing ledger findings, not reopened issues

Revalidation controls use exact retained browser fixture name sequences and require three nonempty recorded 304 rows per browser; malformed or empty fields cannot silently match full expanded literal names
Owned template unit controls spawn no peer/task and perform no request send; client/builder construction is synchronous and returned owners drop lexically; no socket teardown claim is inferred
